meta.name: Latin Master Morphology + Direct Translation Rulepack
meta.description: Unified Latin morphology dataset (nouns/adjectives/pronouns/verbs) + direct-translation rules + regex/assembly helpers.

neuterIdentityRule.description: Neuters: nom=acc=voc in both sg and pl (within their declension/adjective pattern).

notes: Locative -ae is productive mainly for cities/small islands; otherwise rare.
Some masculine 1st declension nouns exist (esp. professions/ethnics), lexicon-driven.
Greek loans/names vary; keep lexicon exceptions as overrides.

erStemRule.note: Some -er nouns drop e in oblique stem (ager/agr-), others keep (puer/puer-). Lexicon decides.

pl.note: Often regular 2nd declension plural; keep lexicon alternates.

notes: Greek accusative -on may appear alongside Latinized -um.
Nom/Voc sg is lexicon-driven; cannot be derived reliably from endings alone.
Acc sg sometimes = nom sg (esp. some i-stems/Greek); keep as variant.
Many 4th declension nouns are feminine (e.g., manus); gender must be lexicon-aware.
dies is often masculine (sometimes feminine); res is typically feminine.
Some words show -e/-ei variation; store lexicon alternates if needed.
Use noun endings with gender selection; stem behavior for -er is lexicon-driven.
Present participles behave like one-termination adjectives with stem in -nt-.
Possessives are adjectives (agree with possessed noun).
Interrogatives share many forms with relatives; engine should treat as separate lexeme class.
1st conj perfect stems often -av-; treat as lexicon-preferred, not mandatory.

eo.note: Present system is irregular (eunt, ibam/ibo...). Store full table if generating.

fio.note: Present system functions as passive of facio.

miscRules.note: Perfect forms can carry present meaning; map tense meanings accordingly in glossing.

greekNounsInLatin.overview: Greek loan nouns may preserve Greek alternates (esp. voc/acc sg). Treat as optional variants.
notes: Names can be mixed Greek+Latin forms; keep both if lexicon flags them.

pronounAdjectives.note: Decline like 1st/2nd adjective except gen sg -ius, dat sg -i.

selectedIrregularNouns.note: Mixed 2nd/4th behavior; allow alternative paradigms if lexicon marks.
Irregular; limited sg; plural vires/virium etc. Lexicon table recommended.

agreementRules.description: Adjectives agree with head nouns in case/number/gender; possessives behave as adjectives.

coordinationRules.description: Coordinated nominals typically share syntactic role; propagate shared features if enabled.

profiles.description: No bracketed context; no overlay rules; morphology+gloss only.
Direct translation plus optional transfer/overlay rules; outputs multiple variants.

rules.description: If a coordinated sex-pair includes a diminutive-marked male lexeme, allow 'young' to transfer to both members unless blocked.
If ark-loading logistics are explicitly in scope, emit a bracketed optional variant: animals are the youngest of their kind.

emitVariant.note: Optional variant only; never replaces literal content.

rules.description: In explicit sexual-prohibition domain, allow masculus/arsen/zachar sense variants mapping to 'young male/child' in alternates.
Brackets may only be inserted by explicit rules; capped per sentence; always optional variants.

variantModel.description: Each sentence yields N variants: morphology disambiguation + sense choices + optional bracket insertions.

regexAndAssembly.priorityRule: Longest suffix match first; if ties, return multiple analyses.

notes: Apply after normalization and punctuation stripping.
Maintain a blocklist for stems where -que/-ve/-ne is lexical (lexicon overrides).

stemDerivation.rule: Use genSg to derive stem when available (3rd).
For 1st/2nd/4th/5th, stem is often lemma minus nomSg ending; lexicon best.

nouns.neuterIdentity: If gender=n, force acc=voc=nom for a chosen number.

verbs.imperfectSubjRule: active: infinitive + personal endings; passive: infinitive + passive endings
verbs.deponentRule: Parse as passive morphology; gloss as active semantics.

meta.name: latinMasterMorph
notes: Inflection rules here are paradigm-first (stable).
Perfect stems and perfect passive participles are lexical; this JSON supplies universal endings and periphrastic patterns, but not stem formation rules.
Macrons are omitted; treat vowel length as optional metadata if you add it later.

neuterRule.statement: Neuter nouns have nom=voc=acc; in plural, nom/acc/voc are typically -a (or -ia for many i-stems).

notes: -abus is rare; include for ambiguity generation.

notes: dies is often masculine; keep gender lexical if you care.

perfectSystem.lexicalNote: perfectStem and ppp must be provided by lexicon or principal parts; do not infer them purely from conjugation class.

voiceNotes: Deponent verbs: passive morphology with active meaning (treat as candidate readings).
Semi-deponent: active present system, deponent-like perfect system.

notes: Often treated as 3rd declension neuter in Latinized forms.

Optional; varies with latinization level.

buildHints: You can invert noun endings by iterating declensions->cases->numbers and mapping ending->feature set list.
For verbs, invert by iterating verb classes->mood->voice->tense->personSlots and mapping ending->feature set list.
ambiguityNotes: Many endings collide across cases/numbers (e.g., -ae, -is, -um). Always return sets, not single tags.
3rd declension stem extraction from nominative is unreliable without genitive or lexicon.

verbFormAlternates.note: Some traditions allow -are alongside -aris for 1st conjugation present passive 2sg.
Perfect active indicative 3pl may appear as -ere (alongside -erunt).

assemblyHints.pattern: present/imperfect passive often render naturally as 'is/was {pastParticiple}' or progressive 'is/was being {pastParticiple}' depending on context
assemblyHints.note: This keeps your existing {ppp} placeholder usable as an English past-participle token.
